articles.headline: No. 3 Louisville women use 26-0 run to ease past Alaska Anchorage 113-40 in Great Alaska Shootout
articles.description: — Elif Istanbulluoglu scored 19 points, Imari Berry had 13 of her 16 in the first quarter, and No. 3 Louisville used a big third-quarter run to ease past Alaska Anchorage 113-40 on Saturday night in the Great Alaska Shootout.

articles.headline: NCAA to scrap pregame handshakes at women's tourney after Auriemma-Staley spat
articles.description: The NCAA will encourage but no longer mandate pregame handshakes between head coaches at the women's tournament after last season's controversy involving Geno Auriemma and Dawn Staley.

articles.headline: Harpring scores 20, No. 24 North Carolina women pull away from Alabama

article.headline: Ajsa Sivka scores 32 in 3rd collegiate game to lead No. 14 Kentucky women over No. 25 NC State 93-78
article.description: — Ajsa Sivka scored 32 points and matched a program record with eight 3-pointers in her third collegiate game, and 14th-ranked Kentucky breezed to a 93-78 victory over No. 25 N.C. State on Sunday at the fourth annual Ally Tipoff.

article.story: CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- — Ajsa Sivka scored 32 points and matched a program record with eight 3-pointers in her third collegiate game, and 14th-ranked Kentucky breezed to a 93-78 victory over No. 25 N.C. State on Sunday at the fourth annual Ally Tipoff. Sivka, a 6-foot-5 guard from Slovenia, made 11 of 17 shots for the Wildcats (3-0) at the double-header event that features top-ranked programs. She sank 8 of 12 from 3-point range and snagged five rebounds. Sivka's eight makes from distance matched Rhyne Howard's single-game school record. Clara Strack totaled 24 points on 10-for-15 shooting for Kentucky with eight rebounds, four assists and two blocks. Savvy Swords pitched in with 14 points off the bench. Khamil Pierre led the Wolfpack (2-1) with 34 points. The senior, who scored a career-high 42 points as a sophomore, made 12 of 25 shots and 9 of 13 free throws. Zoe Brooks went 11 for 13 at the foul line and scored 13. The Wildcats outscored N.C. State 27-20 in the second quarter to turn a five-point first-quarter lead into a 56-44 advantage at halftime. Kentucky cooled off in the second half but still shot 53% overall. The Wildcats made 18 of 39 from beyond the arc (46%), while the Wolfpack shot 3 for 11 from distance. N.C. State dominated in the paint, outscoring Kentucky 34-20 and the Wolfpack turned 15 turnovers by the Wildcats into 13 points. Kentucky scored six points off five N.C. State miscues. Up next Kentucky: Hosts Evansville on Wednesday. N.C. State: Hosts Liberty on Wednesday. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full college basketball coverage here
